item.subject: science
item.stem:
Meera places a concave mirror facing the Sun outside her home in Jaipur. The reflected sunlight forms a small bright spot on a piece of paper, and the paper starts to smoke.
Why does the concave mirror make the paper hot enough to smoke?

options.A: The mirror absorbs the sunlight and becomes hot, and the paper touching the mirror's surface gets heated.
options.B: The mirror spreads the sunlight evenly over the paper, so the whole sheet slowly warms up.
options.C: The mirror is curved inward, so it converges the reflected sunlight into a small spot where concentrated energy raises the temperature.
options.D: The mirror reflects light without any focusing, but paper always catches fire when sunlight falls on it.
